newsitem.title: JAPAN: Key 30-yr U.S. T-bond plunges to 101-5/32 in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Key 30-yr U.S. T-bond plunges to 101-5/32 in Tokyo.

text.p: The key 6-3/4 percent 30-year U.S. Treasury bond had plunged more than half a point from its New York close to 101-5/32 by early afternoon Tokyo on Thursday in response to the fall of the dollar, traders said.
The 30-year bond finished New York trade at 101-23/32 on Wednesday.
The bond was put under strong selling pressure following a steep dive of the dollar against the yen after comments by Ministry of Finance (MOF) official Eisuke Sakakibara.

The action in the currency market began in early Tokyo with Sakakibara quoted in the Nikkei Financial Daily as saying that the correction of last year's dollar plunge against the yen was about to finish. The newspaper had also quoted him as saying that MOF was not trying to push the yen down further.

Sakakibara, director general of MOF's International Finance Bureau, later told Reuters that the ministry was closely watching current developments in the foreign exchange market, but declined to comment either on specific currency levels or the newspaper article.
The market took this as a signal that the ministry is not keen to see further greenback gains and began selling it aggressively.
"The Treasury bond market has been dragged down by strong sales, mainly seen in the futures market," one trader said.
